title: GDScript hot-reload leaves newly added Dictionary/Array members as Nil on live instances
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.6.2-stable.

### System information

Observed during editor GDScript hot reload / live-instance migration. The issue is not tied to fresh instance construction.

### Issue description

When a GDScript is hot-reloaded while existing live instances are still using the old script layout, newly introduced typed built-in members with empty default initializers can be visible in `get_property_list()` but remain stored as `Variant::NIL` on those migrated instances.

Fresh instances created after the reload initialize the same fields correctly. The issue appears specific to live-instance migration during hot reload.

Related: #97834 / #98221 cover a similar hot-reload Nil member case for Callable/lambda initializers. This report is for typed built-in `Dictionary` / `Array` defaults on migrated live instances.

### Example

Start with v1:

```gdscript
extends RefCounted

func describe() -> String:
    return "v1"
```

Create and keep a live instance from v1, then hot-reload the same script resource to v2:

```gdscript
extends RefCounted

var injected_dict: Dictionary = {}
var injected_array: Array = []

func describe() -> String:
    return "dict=%d array=%d" % [injected_dict.keys().size(), injected_array.size()]
```

After reload, on the existing v1-created instance:

```gdscript
print(instance.get_property_list()) # includes injected_dict and injected_array
print(typeof(instance.get("injected_dict"))) # expected TYPE_DICTIONARY, actual TYPE_NIL
print(instance.call("describe")) # expected "dict=0 array=0"; can crash before the fix
```

### Expected behavior

Migrated live instances should initialize newly added typed built-in members to the same non-NIL empty container defaults used by fresh instances in this repro, so `injected_dict` is an empty `Dictionary` and `injected_array` is an empty `Array`.

### Actual behavior

The new property is present, but the backing value is `NIL` on migrated live instances. Calling a `Dictionary` method such as `.keys()` can crash.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

The linked PR adds an engine-level regression test that reproduces the v1-to-v2 hot-reload migration path.
